books.edition: Reprint 2026-27 (First Edition December 2006; Revised Edition November 2022; reprinted January 2026)

source.method: chapter titles from the book's Contents page; topics from each chapter PDF's numbered section and subsection headings, using the headings printed in the chapter body where they differ from the chapter's opening outline (Summary and Exercises are not topics; small neighbouring subsections are grouped; long sections are split at the run-in headings the book prints, such as 'Microsporogenesis :' or 'Agents of Pollination :', or at the parts the section itself names)

topics.title: Flower - A Fascinating Organ of Angiosperms

Student can explain how a selectable marker such as antibiotic resistance helps pick transformed cells
visualIdeas: bacteria growing on ampicillin plates

topics.title: Obtaining the Foreign Gene Product
objectives: Student can explain recombinant proteins and the need for large-scale production
Student can describe stirred-tank bioreactors and the conditions they maintain
visualIdeas: stirred-tank bioreactor with labelled parts

topics.title: Downstream Processing
objectives: Student can describe downstream processing: separation, purification and formulation of the product
Student can explain the need for quality control and clinical trials before marketing
visualIdeas: flow from bioreactor to purified, packaged product

topics.title: Biotechnological Applications in Agriculture
objectives: Student can compare the three options for increasing food production: agrochemicals, organic agriculture and genetically engineered crops
Student can list the benefits of genetically modified (GM) plants, including golden rice rich in vitamin A
visualIdeas: three paths to more food production

topics.title: Bt Cotton
objectives: Student can explain how Bt toxin from Bacillus thuringiensis kills insects but not the bacterium itself
Student can explain how cry genes are introduced into crops such as cotton to make them pest resistant
visualIdeas: Bt cotton boll versus a boll damaged by bollworm

topics.title: Pest Resistant Plants
objectives: Student can explain RNA interference (RNAi) as a method of cellular defence
Student can describe how tobacco plants were made resistant to the nematode Meloidogyne incognita using RNAi
visualIdeas: dsRNA silencing nematode mRNA inside a root

topics.title: Genetically Engineered Insulin
objectives: Student can explain the structure of insulin with A and B chains and the C peptide in proinsulin
Student can describe how Eli Lilly produced human insulin using rDNA technology in E. coli
visualIdeas: two chains of insulin joined by disulphide bridges

topics.title: Gene Therapy
objectives: Student can define gene therapy
Student can describe the first gene therapy for adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency
visualIdeas: lymphocytes receiving a functional ADA gene and returned to the patient

topics.title: Molecular Diagnosis
objectives: Student can explain why early diagnosis needs molecular techniques
Student can describe the use of PCR, recombinant DNA probes and ELISA in diagnosis
visualIdeas: ELISA plate with coloured wells

topics.title: Transgenic Animals
objectives: Student can define transgenic animals and explain why they are produced
Student can give examples of their uses, such as the transgenic cow Rosie producing human protein-enriched milk and testing vaccine and chemical safety
visualIdeas: transgenic cow Rosie

topics.title: Ethical Issues
objectives: Student can explain the role of the Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee (GEAC)
Student can discuss patents on biological resources and biopiracy, with the example of basmati rice
visualIdeas: map of India with basmati growing regions

topics.title: Population Attributes
objectives: Student can define a population and its attributes: birth rate, death rate and sex ratio
Student can interpret age pyramids for expanding, stable and declining populations
Student can explain different ways of measuring population density
visualIdeas: three age pyramids with pre-reproductive, reproductive and post-reproductive bands

topics.title: Population Growth
objectives: Student can explain how natality, mortality, immigration and emigration change population density
Student can write the equation Nt+1 = Nt + [(B + I) - (D + E)]
visualIdeas: population box with arrows in and out for B, I, D and E

topics.title: Growth Models and Life History Variation
objectives: Student can describe exponential growth with dN/dt = rN and the J-shaped curve
Student can describe logistic growth with carrying capacity K and the S-shaped curve
Student can explain how populations evolve life history traits to maximise reproductive fitness
visualIdeas: J-shaped and S-shaped growth curves with K marked

topics.title: Population Interactions: Predation
objectives: Student can list the types of population interactions and their effects on each species
Student can explain the roles of predators in transferring energy, controlling prey and maintaining species diversity
Student can describe defences of prey against predators
visualIdeas: table of interactions with + and - signs
monarch butterfly avoided by a bird

topics.title: Population Interactions: Competition
objectives: Student can explain interspecific competition and Gause's competitive exclusion principle
Student can explain resource partitioning as a way species avoid competition
visualIdeas: warblers feeding at different parts of the same tree

topics.title: Population Interactions: Parasitism, Commensalism and Mutualism
objectives: Student can describe ectoparasites, endoparasites and brood parasitism, as in the cuckoo
Student can describe commensalism with examples such as an orchid on a mango branch and barnacles on whales
Student can describe mutualism in lichens, mycorrhizae and the fig and wasp relationship
visualIdeas: fig flower pollinated by a wasp

topics.title: Ecosystem - Structure and Function
objectives: Student can describe an ecosystem as a functional unit with biotic and abiotic components, using a pond as an example
Student can explain vertical stratification and list the functions of an ecosystem: productivity, decomposition, energy flow and nutrient cycling
visualIdeas: pond ecosystem with producers, consumers and decomposers

topics.title: Productivity
objectives: Student can define primary production and productivity
Student can distinguish gross primary productivity, net primary productivity and secondary productivity
visualIdeas: GPP minus respiration equals NPP bar

topics.title: Decomposition
objectives: Student can describe the steps of decomposition: fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification and mineralisation
Student can explain how chemical composition of detritus and climatic factors affect the rate of decomposition
visualIdeas: leaf litter broken down in steps into humus and minerals

topics.title: Energy Flow
objectives: Student can explain that only a small part of incident solar radiation (photosynthetically active radiation) is captured by plants
Student can describe grazing and detritus food chains, food webs and trophic levels
Student can explain the 10 per cent law of energy transfer and standing crop
visualIdeas: energy flow through trophic levels with decreasing arrows

topics.title: Ecological Pyramids
objectives: Student can construct pyramids of number, biomass and energy
Student can explain why the pyramid of energy is always upright while some pyramids of number and biomass are inverted
Student can state the limitations of ecological pyramids
visualIdeas: upright energy pyramid beside an inverted pyramid of biomass in the sea

topics.title: Biodiversity
objectives: Student can define biodiversity as the term popularised by Edward Wilson for diversity at all levels of biological organisation
Student can describe genetic, species and ecological diversity with examples
visualIdeas: three levels of biodiversity illustrated

topics.title: How Many Species are there on Earth and How Many in India?
objectives: Student can estimate the number of species recorded and the estimated global total
Student can state India's share of global species diversity as a megadiversity country
visualIdeas: pie chart of species by taxonomic group

topics.title: Patterns of Biodiversity
objectives: Student can explain the latitudinal gradient in diversity and the reasons tropics are richer in species
Student can describe the species-area relationship of Humboldt and the meaning of its slope
visualIdeas: species richness against area on log-log axes

topics.title: The Importance of Species Diversity to the Ecosystem
objectives: Student can explain how communities with more species tend to be more stable and productive
Student can explain the rivet popper hypothesis
visualIdeas: aeroplane losing rivets as an analogy for species loss

topics.title: Loss of Biodiversity
objectives: Student can describe the IUCN Red List and recent extinctions
Student can explain the effects of biodiversity loss
Student can explain the four major causes ("the evil quartet"): habitat loss, over-exploitation, alien species invasions and co-extinctions
visualIdeas: four panels for the evil quartet

topics.title: Biodiversity Conservation: Why Should We Conserve Biodiversity?
objectives: Student can explain the narrowly utilitarian, broadly utilitarian and ethical reasons for conserving biodiversity
Student can give examples of ecosystem services, such as the oxygen produced by the Amazon forest
visualIdeas: Amazon forest producing oxygen, medicines and food

topics.title: How do we Conserve Biodiversity?
objectives: Student can distinguish in situ conservation (hotspots, protected areas, sacred groves) from ex situ conservation (zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks, cryopreservation)
Student can describe international efforts such as the Earth Summit at Rio de Janeiro and the World Summit on Sustainable Development
visualIdeas: map of biodiversity hotspots including those in India
